item.title: Overview
item.description:
Design Docs#

These are proposed changes to materialize-monitoring.

Opening a non-draft pull request that adds a page here posts a notification to the #rnd-design-docs Slack channel (internal), the same channel the cloud repository notifies. Marking an existing draft pull request ready for review posts the same notification.

Each doc carries a status in its frontmatter, and the list below shows it.

Status Meaning
Draft Under review. The design is not final
Ready Accepted. The work it describes is planned or in progress, and tracked on the roadmap
Shipped Implemented. The doc now records why the design is the way it is

A new doc starts at Draft.

item.title: First-Class Production Loki Infrastructure
item.description:
First-Class Production Loki Infrastructure#

author Heather Lapointe
lastmod 2026-06-28 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
publishdate 2026-06-27 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
status Shipped

This doc captures the design decisions and open questions for shipping a productionalizable Loki inside the materialize-monitoring umbrella chart. It is the design rationale behind the loki subchart wiring in charts/materialize-monitoring/Chart.yaml; day-2 operational procedures (backup/restore, upgrades, migration) will live in customer-facing docs and are only sketched here.

Goals#

Functional requirements, framed as value-first user stories. Each describes what a user needs and why it matters; the Technical BLUF and the sections below describe how we deliver it. Priority tags (Must / Should / Could) are relative to the Production (M2) milestone.

This doc captures the design for the Terraform wrapper on the Roadmap (M4) and for retiring the hand-rolled observability stack that the materialize-terraform-self-managed module ships today. Terraform is deliberately downstream of Helm: the chart stays the full-fidelity surface, and Terraform pins a chart version and supplies the cloud resources around it.

Goals#

Functional requirements, framed as value-first user stories. Each describes what a user needs and why it matters; the Technical BLUF and the sections below describe how we deliver it. Priority tags (Must / Should / Could) are relative to the first shipped version of the module.

item.title: Observability for Bring-Your-Own-Cloud
item.description:
Observability for Bring-Your-Own-Cloud#

author Heather Lapointe
lastmod 2026-08-13 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
publishdate 2026-08-13 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
status Ready

This doc is the BYOC gateway-to-gateway architecture and proposal owed by the Roadmap (DEP-219), and it covers the two rows next to it: the dual-destination pipeline pattern and sanitizing telemetry before control-plane egress.

The shape is centralized monitoring in our management/control plane, fed by an OTLP ingress that customer environments reach with a client certificate shipped in their license. Inside the customer environment, materialize-monitoring deploys as it does for any self-managed install — the full stack, their Grafana, their retention — and a second, reduced copy of telemetry crosses the boundary to us.

item.title: In-cluster TLS and Certificate Authentication
item.description:
In-cluster TLS and Certificate Authentication#

author Heather Lapointe
lastmod 2026-08-16 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
publishdate 2026-08-16 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
status Shipped

This doc is the design for in-cluster mTLS via cert-manager on the Roadmap (DEP-195, OO-M1). It expands the In-cluster TLS and authentication section of the Terraform modules doc into a full proposal and supersedes it; that section stays as the Terraform-side summary and should point here.

The central claim is that this work is about authentication, not encryption. Every hop inside the stack is plaintext HTTP with authType: none today, and turning on one-way TLS would fix the smaller half of that. Inside a cluster the realistic threat is not a passive network tap, it is a workload that can reach the Service and write whatever it likes into Loki and Thanos. Only the client certificate answers that, which is why the deliverable is mTLS on both halves of each hop rather than https:// in the destination URLs.

item.title: Stability Guarantees and Deprecation Policy
item.description:
Stability Guarantees and Deprecation Policy#

author Heather Lapointe
lastmod 2026-08-24 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
publishdate 2026-08-23 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
status Shipped

This doc proposes the stability guarantees and deprecation policy owed by DEP-127 (OO-M1), listed on the Roadmap as the last unbuilt piece of the versioning story. It is a prerequisite for DEP-205 — stamping 1.0 is the moment the guarantees below stop being aspirational — so this should be agreed before that, not alongside it.

item.title: A Tenant-Scoped Query API for Console and Customer Grafana
item.description:
A Tenant-Scoped Query API for Console and Customer Grafana#

agent Claude Opus 5
author Heather Lapointe
lastmod 2026-09-16 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
publishdate 2026-09-16 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
status Ready

This doc proposes that Thanos and Loki — or something that speaks their query languages — become a required part of every Materialize deployment, self-managed and Cloud alike, and that both gain an authenticated read path scoped to exactly one tenant.

Two consumers motivate it, and they are the same feature. The Materialize console stops rendering metrics from SQL against the environment it is describing and issues PromQL and LogQL instead. A customer attaches their own Grafana to a public authenticated endpoint and gets the same data as a Prometheus and a Loki datasource for their environment.

item.title: Alerting in Self-Managed: Evaluation, Routing, and Customer Extension
item.description:
Alerting in Self-Managed: Evaluation, Routing, and Customer Extension#

agent Claude Opus 5
author Heather Lapointe
lastmod 2026-09-25 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
publishdate 2026-09-17 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
status Ready

This doc proposes that a default install of this chart page somebody when Materialize breaks, and describes what has to exist for that sentence to be true.

The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

Three things stand between here and there, and they are independent problems that happen to share a workstream.

item.title: Call-Home: Opt-In Telemetry from Self-Managed to the Control Plane
item.description:
Call-Home: Opt-In Telemetry from Self-Managed to the Control Plane#

agent Claude Opus 5
author Heather Lapointe
lastmod 2026-09-17 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
publishdate 2026-09-17 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
status Ready

This doc proposes call-home for self-managed Materialize: an opt-in channel by which a customer-operated deployment reports a bounded amount of telemetry to a Materialize-operated control plane, so that Materialize can notice and react to problems without holding access to the customer’s cluster.

item.title: Monitoring Materialize's External Dependencies
item.description:
Monitoring Materialize’s External Dependencies#

agent Claude Opus 5
author Heather Lapointe
lastmod 2026-09-20 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
publishdate 2026-09-20 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
status Ready

This doc proposes how materialize-monitoring covers the two services a Materialize deployment cannot run without and does not run itself: the metadata (consensus) database and the object store. It is the design owed by DEP-233 (OO-M2), and it covers the External components row of the infra-* dashboard family, which today reads “object store yes, consensus DB effectively no”.

item.title: Secret Filtering: A Last Line of Defense for Stored and Egressed Logs
item.description:
Secret Filtering: A Last Line of Defense for Stored and Egressed Logs#

agent Claude
author Heather Lapointe
lastmod 2026-09-24 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
publishdate 2026-09-24 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
status Ready

This doc proposes a last line of defense against credentials in logs. Every log line the gateway receives passes a secret filter before it is parsed or stored. Every line bound for a Materialize control plane, over BYOC or call-home, passes a second and stricter filter on its own branch, immediately before the writer. It is the credentials half of DEP-220. The BYOC design applies pattern redaction “as defense in depth rather than as the primary control” and leaves it unspecified; this doc specifies it.
